$comment: The first-party packages this application depends on, the forks it carries and
the overrides it sets. The site's /packages/ page and every package count it
shows are rendered from this file; test/ash_enterprise/site_data_test.exs fails
when it disagrees with mix.exs, mix.lock or battery/mix.exs.
A package is first-party when it is one of our own libraries the build resolves:
a lukegalea/* git dependency in mix.lock that is not a fork, or a path
dependency inside this repository. `declared` says how it arrives: `direct`
(named in mix.exs), `transitive` (only through another package) or `path`.
`ref` must equal the commit mix.lock pins. Moving a dependency fails the test
until someone re-reads that row: `version` and `stated_status` were read from
the package's own mix.exs and README at that commit.
maturity is derived, not judged:
used-and-tested-here  -- lib/ names the package's modules and the application's
own suite (test/) names them too, so CI fails when the
package breaks here.
wired-not-tested-here -- lib/ wires it, but no test file names its modules; it
runs underneath code that is tested, and is tested in
its own repository.
tooling               -- a dev and test dependency. Not in a release.
The test checks the first two against lib/ and test/ by module name (`module`).
`battery` is true when battery/mix.exs declares the package, so CI's
cross-substrate battery job exercises its seams with the others.
`hex_name` was checked against hex.pm on `hex_checked`. `hex_path` and the forks'
paths back are summaries of docs/BLEEDING-EDGE.md, which is the longer account.
Nothing here is published to Hex: every first-party package is git only.

packages.name: ash_a2ui
packages.purpose: Generates A2UI (Agent to UI) 1.0 payloads from Ash resources.
packages.stated_status: Under active development; the first release waits for an npm release of the A2UI renderer that implements the 1.0 specification.
packages.hex_path: No git dependencies of its own.
packages.carry: Tracks the A2UI protocol, so a protocol revision is an update here. Confined to lib/ash_enterprise_web/a2ui/ and one live_session in the router, so removing it is a deletion.

packages.name: ash_acp
packages.purpose: An Agent Client Protocol server adapter: JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio or HTTP, mapped onto behaviours the host declares. Transport and mapping only.
packages.used_for: Approving governed invocations from an ACP client (AshEnterprise.Acp is the host seam).
packages.hex_path: No git dependencies of its own.
packages.carry: Follows the Agent Client Protocol, so a protocol revision is an update here. Authorization stays in the host's Ash policies; the adapter holds no rules of its own.

packages.name: ash_agent
packages.purpose: Governed invocations and durable agent runs: Spark fragments, an effects extension and host behaviours. The host supplies the base resource, data layer, tenancy, policies and triggers.
packages.used_for: The agent runtime: effects declarations on actions, governed invocations with approval, durable runs and steps.
packages.hex_name: taken: an unrelated package of the same name (hex.pm/packages/ash_agent).
packages.hex_path: None planned: reaching Hex would mean renaming the package (ADR 0056).
packages.carry: The host instantiates every resource on its own base, so a fragment change upstream is a host migration here. lib/ names it in more files than any other first-party package.

packages.name: ash_agent_tools
packages.purpose: Read-only Ash introspection for coding agents: describe resources and actions, validate inputs, and explain authorization without running anything.
packages.used_for: Agent tooling in development, and the code subjects the engineering standards are judged over (dev and test only).
packages.hex_name: taken: an unrelated package of the same name (hex.pm/packages/ash_agent_tools).
packages.hex_path: After its optional dependencies (ash_rules, ash_bpmn, ash_decisions, ash_judgments) reach Hex; the name is taken there.
packages.carry: Nothing in a release. Dropping it removes the agent tooling and the standards' code subjects, which compile only when it is loaded.

packages.name: ash_bpmn
packages.purpose: BPMN processes executed by Ash: an embedded bpmn-js designer, a compiler from BPMN XML to an immutable graph snapshot, and a durable token interpreter over Postgres and Oban.
packages.used_for: The process engine: approvals, credentialing cases, recipes that start processes.
packages.stated_status: 0.1.0. The approval layer and the engine are tested against real Postgres.
packages.hex_path: No git dependencies of its own.
packages.carry: Adds columns to resources the host owns, so a bump runs `mix ash.codegen --check` and may need a host migration. Processes in flight keep the version they started on.

packages.name: ash_compliance
packages.purpose: Catalogs, profiles and waivers compiled into immutable ash_rules bundles, with findings projected from an event log and append-only evaluations.
packages.used_for: Compliance bundles and findings, the evidence archive and its verified move, and the audit package's OSCAL assessment results.
packages.carry: Says owned, evidenced or unknown for each criterion; it does not attest. The host works around one packaging bug (its Oban workers are not compiled here), listed in docs/BLEEDING-EDGE.md section 3.

packages.name: ash_decisions
packages.purpose: DMN decisions as versioned Ash resources: a DMN document compiled and verified into an immutable snapshot and evaluated by a native FEEL engine, with a dmn-js designer.
packages.used_for: The decisions a process's business rule tasks route on.
packages.hex_path: No: needs boxic_dmn's trace evaluation upstream first.
packages.carry: Brings the boxic_dmn fork, which validates DMN by calling xmllint, so libxml2 is a runtime dependency. Adds columns to resources the host owns.

packages.name: ash_discrete_business_events
packages.purpose: A business-event ledger: raw source records with temporal version history, a chained append-only event ledger, and mappings kept as data.
packages.used_for: The business-event ledger derived from the canonical store's writes, and the source-record landing master data reads.
packages.hex_path: No: needs an ash_events release carrying the fork's changes.
packages.carry: Depends on the ash_events fork and on temporal resources, which need PostgreSQL 18.

packages.name: ash_events_chain
packages.purpose: A hash chain for an AshEvents event log: chain and immutability triggers, a verifier that reads the hot table and its archive as one chain, and a verified move to the archive.
packages.used_for: The audit log's hash chain, its verifier and its retention move.
packages.hex_path: No git dependencies of its own.
packages.carry: Its triggers live in the database, so a change to the chain is a migration and old rows must still verify.

packages.name: ash_events_projections
packages.purpose: Declarative projectors that fold an AshEvents event log into tables, with checkpoints, dead letters, rebuilds and gap detection.
packages.used_for: The projector engine under compliance findings and data-quality projections.
packages.stated_status: Pre-1.0; the DSL may change between minor versions.
packages.hex_path: No git dependencies of its own.
packages.carry: Arrives through ash_compliance, but the host configures it and mounts its three resources in the compliance domain, so its schema is the host's to migrate.

packages.name: ash_evidence
packages.purpose: Evidence records: immutable document versions, parse runs, and the addressed atoms a run produces. It records; it never calls an instrument.
packages.used_for: The records judgments cite; the host supplies the instruments and the orchestration.
packages.hex_path: No git dependencies of its own.
packages.carry: Declared with `branch: "main"`; mix.lock pins the commit.

packages.name: ash_judgments
packages.purpose: Declared, typed questions over any resource, a judgment ledger that keeps provenance, and bridges from recorded judgments to decision inputs, rule facts and process signals. Ships no model client.
packages.used_for: The judgment layer: questions, the ledger, calibration, and the instrument profiles configured in config/runtime.exs.
packages.carry: Depends on four other first-party packages and both forks, so it moves last. Model calls go through ash_ai and ReqLLM, which the host configures.

packages.name: ash_mdm
packages.purpose: Master data management for Ash: versioned schema mappings as data, deterministic entity resolution with rules as data, survivorship and non-destructive merge over golden records.
packages.used_for: Master data: mappings, matching and the survivorship merge.
packages.carry: Resource macros the host instantiates on its own base, so their schema is the host's to migrate.

packages.name: ash_open_lineage
packages.purpose: Emits OpenLineage 2-0-2 run events for each successful create, update or destroy, with a small API for jobs outside Ash. Facets carry structural names, never actor, tenant or data values.
packages.hex_path: No git dependencies of its own.
packages.carry: Pinned with `ref:` and `override: true`, because ash_discrete_business_events declares it too; the host's pin wins tree-wide.

packages.name: ash_operations
packages.purpose: Declares a provider's HTTP operations on an Ash resource: one generic action per operation, a spec pinned at compile time, one retry table and typed errors.
packages.used_for: The credential registry's connector and the provider webhook ingress.
packages.hex_path: No git dependencies of its own.
packages.carry: Its ADR is still proposed; the credential registry is the one built reference.

packages.name: ash_planning
packages.purpose: A constraint-solving proposal kernel for Ash: backends, IR, validators and resource fragments.
packages.used_for: The planning kernel and its MiniZinc backend through Solverl.
packages.carry: Solving runs through Solverl's MiniZinc backend, bounded by prlimit and Solverl timeouts (ADR 0062).

packages.name: ash_rules
packages.purpose: Declared questions compiled to a serializable, content-hashed rule IR, evaluated per subject or over a set as Ash queries, with in, out and unknown outcomes where missing data is never a pass.
packages.used_for: The rule IR, fact schemas and evaluator under compliance and judgments.
packages.hex_path: No git dependencies of its own.
packages.carry: Bundles are content-hashed, so a change to how the IR is encoded changes their hashes.

packages.name: ash_strangler
packages.purpose: Strangler-fig migrations for Ash: map a resource onto a legacy Postgres schema and move it through the migration phases without hand-written SQL.
packages.used_for: The read model over the legacy schema and the bridge that makes a legacy write visible to LiveView.
packages.hex_path: No git dependencies of its own.
packages.carry: Only needed while a legacy schema is being migrated. It is used by lib/ash_enterprise/legacy/, the user ledger and the platform base's projected-lifecycle verifier.

packages.name: ash_enterprise_telemetry
packages.purpose: Runtime observability for Ash and Phoenix: one setup call that attaches tracing, correlation, background-job context, a browser span ingest and error reporting.
packages.used_for: Tracing, correlation and error reporting in this application.
packages.distribution: git only: a sparse git dependency on this repository (sparse: "telemetry")
packages.hex_path: Not on the BLEEDING-EDGE path: it lives in this repository and has its own mix project, lock and CI job.
packages.carry: Its own suite runs in this repository's CI (the telemetry job); it depends on nothing in the application.

forks.name: ash_events
forks.adds: Upstream main, which records a temporal write's as_of on its event and is unreleased, plus one fix of ours: a data layer's no_rollback error reaches the caller instead of crashing the action wrapper.
forks.path_back: Propose the no_rollback fix upstream; when a release carries both, point every declaring package at Hex and drop the override.

forks.name: boxic_dmn
forks.adds: evaluate_with_trace, which returns the matched rule ids and hit policy with the value: the provenance a decision's audit trail is built on.
forks.path_back: Propose evaluate_with_trace upstream; when a Hex release carries it, ash_decisions moves to Hex and this application only runs mix deps.update.

overrides.name: assent
overrides.reason: ash_authentication 4.x caps assent below 0.3, and EEF-CVE-2026-117656 is fixed only in 0.3.2. The application configures no OAuth strategy, so assent is loaded and never called.
overrides.path_back: Move to the first ash_authentication 5.x release, then drop the override.

tooling_forks.name: expert
tooling_forks.note: A language-server fork used only if an editor or agent is pointed at it. Nothing in mix.exs depends on it.
